ratings_why.fun: Real choice between letting Guises run and cashing them in, but every board means reading other cards' text through yours, so turns are heavy to parse.
ratings_why.distinct: A tribe whose text is mostly copied text, with time worn as a resource and Stocks as bodies without souls, plays unlike any of today's six.

verdict_why: v2 fixed the Seamstress loop and the two-Ladies ruling; what's left is wording polish, and more rounds would change it more than improve it.

points.text: "Guise a unit in the shop" can read as putting a Guise on the shop unit. Writing "Wear the Guise of…" on Foundling, Pip Unlike, Hob's Ring Dancer, Tam Twice and Penny Second would match Glamourer and read at a glance.
The Lady Under the Hill can carry six cards' text. Show each copied card as a small borrowed-coat badge you can tap, not as merged text, so she reads as 'wears every face'.
Worn ticking, Keeper of the Lost Hour and the Hundred-Year Nurse all happen at Start of Turn. One line on Worn saying it ticks first would settle what the Nurse reads.
Say whether a Changeling used up by Tam Twice brings its own buffs into the golden; players will ask before they commit their buffed Stock.
Fetch of the Front Rank is the clearest 'arrives in someone's place' card; a short swap animation at Start of Combat would sell it. Say it does nothing across an empty slot.

standouts.why: Pip Unlike's mirror-backwards copy is the folklore figure as a rule, and the flip is easy to see on the board.
Penny Second tells her whole story in one line: take the duchess's place, send the real one away to the shop.
Exchange Assessor leaves a Stock of the killer in the dead Changeling's slot: 'something left in return', read at a glance.

weakest.why: Keeper of the Lost Hour only bumps a counter; the lost-hour fantasy is in the name, not in what it does.
Tam Twice packs three rules into one card; it is the hardest text in the tribe to read mid-turn.
Alder Carver is a plain half-stat copy that any copy tribe would have.

flags.note: A Stock of the Lady under Wicker Moll gives two or three Ladies; strong and fun, worth the owner's eye.
Golden Wicker Moll makes a full copy of your carry with its text every turn, bounded only by slots.
Tam Twice with Glamourer and Penny Second may chain triples and Discovers fast.
